_comment: Editor default demo scene (step E2, docs/06-editor-roadmap.md) -- opened automatically when no scene path is given on the command line. The Editor's own Scene View doesn't wire a physics callback (read-only load, see engine::scene::LoadScene's own comment), so the "collider"+"rigidbody" pair below spawns cleanly with the ECS components present but no live Jolt body -- it only actually simulates in Play Mode (editor_play, which does wire PhysicsWorld). "isStatic": false here is deliberately not the RigidbodyComponent default (true) -- proves RigidbodyComponent::isStatic (post-Editor-E8) actually round-trips through a Save now, a gap ExtractEntityDescs() used to silently drop a whole "rigidbody" block over (see SceneDocument.h's own comment) -- watch this entity fall under gravity in Play Mode, then Save from the Editor's Scene View and confirm the reloaded file still has "isStatic": false, not vanished or silently reset to the default. "guid" below is assets/m1_cube.glb's actual, committed Asset GUID (see assets/m1_cube.glb.meta). The middle cube's "scripts" array only does anything in Play Mode (editor/play_main.cpp) -- the Editor's own read-only Scene View has no AttachScriptFn wired up, so it just sits there like any other entity when merely viewing/editing this scene. The last entity's "parent": 2 (post-Editor-E8 hierarchy, docs/07-unity-parity-analysis.md) makes it a child of the RotateScript cube -- its own position [1.5,0,0] is local to that parent, so in Play Mode it visibly orbits as the parent spins, proving world-matrix composition through World::GetWorldMatrix() actually works, not just that a parent field exists. That same last entity also carries a "material" block (post-Editor-E8 material assets, renderer/MaterialData.h) -- assets/m_demo_red.material.json's actual, committed GUID (see that file's own .meta sidecar) -- so it renders bright red through ForwardLitColorPipeline instead of ForwardLitPipeline's debug normal-color visualization, proving a material-tinted entity actually looks different, not just that the field round-trips. The final entity referencing m1_cube.glb again (position [4.0, 0.5, 0.0]) references assets/m_demo_checker_tint.material.json's own mesh instead (assets/m7_quad.gltf, deliberately, not an oversight: m1_cube.glb predates TEXCOORD_0 -- see cmake/CookAssets.cmake's own comment -- so every one of its vertices samples a texture at UV (0,0), which would just look like one flat color rather than proving anything) and assets/m_demo_checker_tint.material.json ("ForwardLitTexturedColor" shader) -- a live example of the Texture property type, actually showing M7's own checker pattern (not just a solid sampled color) through the RHITexture/descriptor-set plumbing this feature added to the Editor executables, tinted light blue. Lighting phase A (post-Editor-E8, docs/01 section 8.3): the near-white cube at [4.0, 0.5, 0.0] references assets/m_demo_lit_white.material.json ("ForwardLitShaded" shader) -- unlike every other material-tinted entity in this scene, its visible shading actually comes from the two light entities below it, not from its own tint. A Directional light (no mesh -- lights are Transform-only entities, same as an empty object) with a downward-and-forward rotation acts as "the sun" (ambient + a soft N-dot-L falloff); a warm-orange Point light positioned near that same cube (range 8, so its falloff is visible within the scene's scale) proves both LightComponent::Type values and the Blinn-Phong specular highlight (visible as a brighter spot on the lit cube facing the point light) work, not just the directional case alone. Default-material follow-up (the user's own explicit request, post-lighting-phase-A): the ground plane, the RotateScript cube, and the falling physics box are all *deliberately* left without a "material" block -- since ForwardVertexLitPipeline.h's own comment, they now render through colorPipeline's flat kMissingMaterialColor (editor/main.cpp) instead of ForwardLitPipeline's old debug normal-color visualization, an unmistakable purple/violet proving an entity has no material assigned. The second cube (position [-2, 0.5, 0]) instead references assets/m_demo_vertex_lit.material.json ("ForwardVertexLit" shader) -- this engine's new default/base lit material, same lighting formula as m_demo_lit_white's own "ForwardLitShaded" but evaluated per-vertex, tinted grassy green so the tint is visibly part of the result too. The last entity (position [-4.0, 1.0, -2.5], a second m7_quad.gltf instance next to the unlit checker one) references assets/m_demo_vertex_lit_textured.material.json ("ForwardVertexLitTextured" shader) -- same per-vertex lighting plus the same checker albedo texture m_demo_checker_tint.material.json already uses, proving the "texture if assigned, else tintColor" material family works with a texture actually assigned (see ShaderPropertySchema.h's own comment on why the no-texture case is a separate shader rather than an in-shader branch).
